land.text: Pannonia, the Hunnic land the Ostrogoths held after Attila's sons lost it at Nedao (454)

predecessors.note: The Ostrogoths page: 'independence from the remains of the Hunnic Empire following the death of Attila the Hun in 453'; 'freedom from domination by Attila's sons was confirmed by the Battle of Nedao in 454'; 'first settled in the Pannonian area of Lake Balaton and Sirmium' (undated).

union.text: Dalmatia, annexed by Odoacer after Nepos's murder in 480

land.text: Odoacer's realm at his death: Italy with Sicily but not Sardinia, and Dalmatia

predecessors.note: Odoacer's realm passed to Theodoric in March 493 ('Theodoric ... left him as the master of Italy', Odoacer and Theodoric the Great pages). Sicily and Dalmatia are carried with it by reading (Ostrogoths page: 'Ostrogothic power was fully established over Italy, Sicily, Dalmatia and the lands to the north of Italy', undated, near 500); Sardinia stayed Vandal and the Rugians' land north of the Danube had been settled by the Lombards by 493 (Odoacer page).

land.text: Italy and the lands held with it, from Cliopatria's Ostrogothic Kingdom row

successors.note: The same Goths and the same realm: the Ostrogothic Kingdom and Ostrogoths pages found the kingdom in Italy in 493; Cliopatria splits them at 499/500 and the Ostrogoths row (Q103122) differs from the Kingdom row (Q583038). This dossier keeps Italy for 493-499 (keyframe ostrogoths_493) and ends with a bridging dissolve at 499; the Ostrogothic Kingdom dossier should start at 500 from Cliopatria's row and take the land from here. If its author starts it at 493 instead, trim this dossier to 492 and move the 493 events (rename, the three gains from kingdom-of-odoacer) there.

capitals.name: Ravenna
capitals.note: Ostrogothic Kingdom page: 'Ravenna (493-540)'; 'By 493 Ravenna was taken, where Theodoric would set up his capital' (Ostrogoths page). No seat is named for 454-492.

rulers.name: Theodemir
rulers.note: Theodemir page infobox 469-475 ('Theodemir died in 475'); the Ostrogoths page has him dying at Cyrrhus in 474. His brothers-in-law Valamir and Videmir are not dated on the pages.

rulers.name: Theodoric the Great
rulers.note: King of the Ostrogoths from 475 ('Theoderic fully succeeded him in 475'), co-king from 471; king in Italy 493-526 (state ends here at 499 for Cliopatria's row).

correction.text: Pannonia, the 455 shape (Hungary, Croatia, Bosnia, west Serbia and east Austria)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 454: the Ostrogoths' independence ('following the death of Attila the Hun in 453', confirmed at Nedao in 454). Cliopatria's first shape starts in 455; it is used a year earlier. The pages place the Goths 'in the Pannonian area of Lake Balaton and Sirmium', undated.

138,269 km2 for 455-475. Theodemir page: 'In 469, a Roman imperial army was defeated and chased away from Pannonia'; the Ostrogoths page: Theodemir 'brought these Goths into East Roman territory in 473/474'. So the Pannonian shape holds until 473. No infobox area on either page.

138,291 km2 in Pannonia for 476-479, but the Goths had left in 473/474; 'About 476 ... The Amal-led kingdom was based on the Lower Danube in Moesia' (Ostrogoths page). Moesia is the shape for 474-478.

correction.text: Epirus 479-482 and the Lower Danube (Moesia) 483-488; years 479-488

keyframe_review.note: 138,200 km2 in Pannonia for 480-489 is 6-15 years late. Theodoric the Great page: 'settled his people in Epirus in 479', raided Greece in 482, 'commanded the Danubian provinces of Dacia Ripensis and Moesia Inferior' in 483, blockaded Constantinople in 487 and set out for Italy in autumn 488. The shape to use is Epirus (479-482) and the Lower Danube provinces (483-488); the union is the coarse form.

correction.text: the ground between the Isonzo and Verona, held after the victories of August-September 489

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 489: the Ostrogoths cross the Julian Alps and win at the Isonzo (28 August) and at Verona (September); Cliopatria has no 489 Italian shape. A 150 km disc round Verona is the ground the pages name; Odoacer holds Ravenna and the rest.

correction.text: northern Italy but for Ravenna: Cliopatria's 490 shape inside Italy (the Po plain and the Alps) less Ravenna's province

keyframe_review.note: Year 490 only; 491-492 and 493-499 are the two keyframes that follow. Cliopatria's 417,631 km2 is Italy plus Austria, Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Dalmatia, the last four being the old Pannonian shape carried forward; the pages date Pannonia to 504-505 (Theodoric the Great page), so only the northern part inside Italy is kept (119,116 km2 without Ravenna). The Odoacer page says Theodoric 'seized most of Italy by 490' but names only Milan, Pavia and Ticinum, all in the north, and not Rome or the south; Odoacer is besieged in Ravenna from after the Adda (11 August 490) to 5 March 493. The south therefore stays in the contested zone (contest_start 489 to contest_end 493) and is not drawn as Gothic. An earlier version of this verdict carried the 490 shape inside Italy (120,380 km2, southern edge 43.76 N) to 499, which left out Rome, the south and Sicily for 493-499.

union.text: northern Italy but for Ravenna: Cliopatria's 490 shape inside Italy (the Po plain and the Alps) less Ravenna's province
Lilybaeum, the toehold in western Sicily

correction.text: northern Italy but for Ravenna, plus Lilybaeum (Marsala) in western Sicily, ceded by the Vandals in 491

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 491-492: the 490 northern shape plus Lilybaeum. Gaiseric page footnote: Sicily 'was ceded in 476 to Odoacer except for a toehold on the far west coast, Lilybaeum, which was ceded in 491 to Theodoric'. A 40 km disc round Marsala (about 1,260 km2) detached from the north; the rest of Italy and Sicily stay with Odoacer or contested.

union.text: Dalmatia, annexed by Odoacer after Nepos's murder in 480

correction.text: Odoacer's realm at his death: Italy with Sicily but not Sardinia, and Dalmatia

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 493-499: Odoacer's realm in Theodoric's hands. Italy less Sardinia (Vandal) is 264,028 km2 and Dalmatia 29,842 km2 (about 294,000 km2 together); the Italian part is 1.07 times the 246,830 km2 that Cliopatria's Ostrogothic Kingdom 500 shape holds inside Italy, where the earlier 120,380 km2 was a factor of 2.05 short. Pages: Theodoric 'master of Italy' after 15 March 493 (Theodoric the Great page); 'Ostrogothic power was fully established over Italy, Sicily, Dalmatia and the lands to the north of Italy' (Ostrogoths page, undated, near 500). No page dates the passing of Sicily or Dalmatia (both Odoacer's before 493) or of Raetia and Noricum, which are left out; the Rugians' land north of the Danube had been settled by the Lombards by 493 (Odoacer page). Pannonia and Sirmium come only in 504-505 and Provence in 508, both after this dossier. No infobox area on the Ostrogoths page (checked again on 2026-10-19).

region.text: Pannonia: the Balaton and Sirmium country

ledger.note: 454: the Ostrogoths are free. 'independence from the remains of the Hunnic Empire following the death of Attila the Hun in 453' and 'freedom from domination by Attila's sons was confirmed by the Battle of Nedao in 454' (the Nedao page: they were 'eventually becoming federates of the Eastern Roman Empire'; their part in the battle is disputed). The Amal Goths 'apparently first settled in the Pannonian area of Lake Balaton and Sirmium'; the pages do not date the settlement.

474: the Goths leave Pannonia. Theodemir 'brought these Goths into East Roman territory in 473/474' (Ostrogoths page). Cliopatria keeps the Pannonian shape to 489; the pages do not say who held Pannonia next (the Gepids held Sirmium by 504, Ostrogothic Kingdom page).

region.text: the Lower Danube in Moesia, East Roman territory

ledger.note: 473/474: the Goths settle on East Roman soil as federates, not as conquerors. 'Theodemir ... brought these Goths into East Roman territory in 473/474'; 'About 476 ... His kingdom, now based on the Lower Danube in Moesia, was recognized as a federate kingdom and granted (at least in theory) an annual subsidy' (Ostrogoths page). The page dates the recognition to about 476, so 474-475 is the entry and the tint is drawn from 474; the Theodoric the Great page calls them 'foederati or federates of the Roman army' without a date. eastern-roman-empire dates its mirror vassal_start to 483 and has no loss in 474: the Empire keeps the land. Replaces the earlier 'gain' of 474.

479: Epirus. 'Theodoric settled his people in Epirus in 479 with the help of his relative Sidimund.' A federate settlement on imperial soil, like Moesia, not a cession: eastern-roman-empire has no 479 loss. The page does not say when the Goths left Epirus (raid on Greece and Larissa 482, command of Dacia Ripensis and Moesia Inferior 483), so the region is held coarsely to 488. Replaces the earlier 'gain' of 479.

region.text: the Lower Danube in Moesia, East Roman territory

ledger.note: autumn 488: the Goths march for Italy. 'Theodoric then moved with his people towards Italy in the autumn of 488' (Theodoric the Great page); the Ostrogoths page: he 'set out in 488, by commission from the Byzantine emperor Zeno, to recover Italy from Odoacer'. The Danubian provinces stay East Roman; eastern-roman-empire's vassal_end 488 is the mirror. Replaces the earlier 'loss'.
autumn 488: the same march ends the federate settlement in Epirus (held coarsely from 479, see the 479 event).

28 August 489: the Ostrogoths cross the Julian Alps. 'In 489, Theodoric led the Ostrogoths across the Julian Alps and into Italy'; 'On 28 August, Odoacer met him at the Isonzo, only to be defeated'; Verona followed in September. The Ostrogoths page: 'the Rugii ... joined the Ostrogoths in their invasion of Italy'.

region.text: northern Italy but for Ravenna (the Po plain and the Alps)

ledger.note: 11 August 490: the Adda. After the victory on the Adda 'Odoacer was forced back into Ravenna, where Theodoric besieged him'; Theodoric was 'defeated by Odoacer's forces at Faenza' earlier in 490 (Theodoric the Great page). The Odoacer page says Theodoric 'seized most of Italy by 490' and names only Milan, Pavia and Ticinum, so the gain is drawn as the northern shape of Cliopatria's 490 row (119,116 km2 without Ravenna's province); Rome and the south are not named and stay contested until March 493. kingdom-of-odoacer has no mirrored loss.

region.text: Lilybaeum, the toehold in western Sicily

ledger.note: 491: Lilybaeum goes to Theodoric. Gaiseric page footnote: Sicily 'was ceded in 476 to Odoacer except for a toehold on the far west coast, Lilybaeum, which was ceded in 491 to Theodoric'; no month. The Vandal Kingdom page: Gunthamund 'lost large parts of Sicily to Theodoric's Ostrogoths' (no year, Lilybaeum not named); the Odoacer page has the Vandals invading Sicily in 490; the Ostrogothic Kingdom page is silent. vandal-kingdom /ledger/11 is the mirror loss.
493: the capital is Ravenna (Ostrogothic Kingdom page: 'Ravenna (493-540)').

493: Theodoric founds the Ostrogothic Kingdom in Italy. 'in 493 founded the Ostrogothic Kingdom in Italy after defeating Odoacer' (Ostrogoths page); the Emperor Anastasius recognised him in 497 ('patricius and viceroy', Ostrogothic Kingdom page). The same people and the same colour continue to 499 here; Cliopatria's 'Ostrogothic Kingdom' row starts at 500.

minus.text: Lilybaeum, the toehold in western Sicily

region.text: Sicily but for Lilybaeum, Gothic since 491

ledger.note: 493: Sicily follows Odoacer's realm to Theodoric (bridging). Odoacer had it from autumn 476 (Gaiseric page: 'He gave Sicily to Odoacer in 476'); the Vandals invaded in 490 (Odoacer page); 'Ostrogothic power was fully established over Italy, Sicily, Dalmatia and the lands to the north of Italy' around 500 (Ostrogoths page). No page dates the passing of Sicily, so 493 is the year Odoacer's realm ended, not a dated event.

region.text: Dalmatia, annexed by Odoacer after Nepos's murder in 480

ledger.note: 493: Dalmatia follows Odoacer's realm to Theodoric (bridging). Odoacer 'invaded Dalmatia, executed the conspirators, and annexed the region within two years' of 480 (Odoacer page); the Ostrogoths page lists Dalmatia in the Ostrogothic power around 500, undated; the Ostrogothic Kingdom page says only that the Goths 'passed through Dalmatia' in 488. No page dates the passing.

region.text: Ravenna and the rest of Italy south of the Gothic line of 490: Tuscany, Rome, Campania, Apulia and Calabria; not Sardinia or Sicily

ledger.note: 5 March 493: Theodoric enters Ravenna and becomes master of Italy. 'By 493 Ravenna was taken' (Ostrogoths page); 'Theodoric entered Ravenna on 5 March 493' and killed Odoacer on 15 March, 'making him the master of Italy' (Theodoric the Great page); the Odoacer page dates the treaty to 25 February (the Theodoric page: 2 February) and Odoacer's killing to 15 March. The region is Italy less Sardinia and Sicily and less the northern shape Gothic since 490 (121,139 km2); the pages name no city of the centre or south in 489-493, so the extent is the country's, kingdom-of-odoacer's hand-over of all Italy. Replaces the earlier gain of Ravenna alone.
March 493: the war for Italy ends. Odoacer 'was killed by Theodoric's own hand' at a banquet on 15 March; Italy is Theodoric's.

union.text: Dalmatia, annexed by Odoacer after Nepos's murder in 480

region.text: Odoacer's realm at his death: Italy with Sicily but not Sardinia, and Dalmatia

ledger.note: 499: Cliopatria's Ostrogoths row ends and its Ostrogothic Kingdom row begins at 500. The pages show no break (the Kingdom 'controlled Italy and neighbouring areas between 493 and 553', Ostrogothic Kingdom page); this is a bridging end, not a conquest, and the land handed on is the 493-499 shape (Italy with Sicily, and Dalmatia). The Ostrogothic Kingdom dossier is not written yet: it should start at 500 and take this land; the 493-499 years are kept here.

wars.name: Battle of Nedao
wars.outcome: Hunnic dominance in Central and Eastern Europe is broken; the Ostrogoths gain independence by the early 460s and later become federates of the Eastern Roman Empire. Their part in the battle is disputed (Jordanes says they fought the Huns, modern scholars doubt it).
wars.note: Ardaric's Gepids led the allied subject peoples; the Gepids had no Cliopatria row before 510.

wars.name: Battle of Bolia
belligerents: opponent not named on the Ostrogoths page
wars.outcome: 'Eventual Gothic victory at the Battle of Bolia in 469, now under Theodemir'; the Theodemir page: 'a Roman imperial army was defeated and chased away from Pannonia' in 469.

wars.name: Gothic wars in the Balkans
wars.outcome: Theodoric Strabo is declared king in 473; the Amal Goths settle in Epirus (479), raid Greece and sack Larissa (482), command Dacia Ripensis and Moesia Inferior (483), blockade Constantinople (487) and march for Italy on Zeno's commission (autumn 488).

wars.name: Ostrogothic defeat of the Gepids at Sirmium
wars.outcome: The Gepids were 'defeated at Sirmium in August 489' on the way to Italy; the Goths took Pannonia and Sirmium only in 504-505.

wars.name: Odoacer-Theodoric war
wars.outcome: Isonzo (28 August 489), Verona (September 489), Faenza (a defeat, 490), the Adda (11 August 490); a siege of Ravenna to the treaty of February 493, Theodoric's entry on 5 March and Odoacer's killing on 15 March.
wars.note: Odoacer page; the Theodoric the Great page gives the treaty as 2 February, the Odoacer page 25 February.

certainty.note: A migrating people on federate land: Pannonia, Moesia and Epirus were never bounded by a frontier line.

Italy's limits are those of Odoacer's kingdom; the page names no surveyed frontier. The 491-492 Lilybaeum patch, the Sicily and Dalmatia of 493-499 and the whole southern extent are readings (confidence 1-2).

sources.title: Theodoric the Great

sources.note: Capital Ravenna 493-540, the kingdom 493-553, recognition 497. Re-read 2026-10-19: silent on how Sicily and Dalmatia passed; 'controlled Italy and neighbouring areas between 493 and 553'.

sources.note: Reign 469-475, Roman army chased from Pannonia 469, Theodoric's hostage years.

sources.title: Odoacer

Re-read 2026-10-19: 'seized most of Italy by 490' (Milan, Pavia, Ticinum named), three-year siege to 5 March 493, Sicily 476 and the Vandal invasion of 490, Dalmatia annexed within two years of 480.

sources.note: 454; Ostrogoths among the peoples who gained independence; Pannonia not mentioned.

notes: Cliopatria's 455-489 Ostrogoths shape is a Pannonian settlement (138,000 km2), but the pages have the Goths in East Roman territory from 473/474 (Moesia on the Lower Danube, Epirus 479, Dacia Ripensis and Moesia Inferior 483), so the 476 and 480 shapes are marked wrong and replaced by Moesia and Epirus. The 490 shape adds Italy to the old Pannonian land; only the northern part inside Italy is kept for 490-492 (ostrogoths_490, ostrogoths_491) and Odoacer's realm, Italy with Sicily and Dalmatia, for 493-499 (ostrogoths_493). Ostrogoths (Q103122, 455-499) and Ostrogothic Kingdom (Q583038, 500-560) are different Cliopatria Names and different Wikidata items, but the pages show one people and one realm: the kingdom in Italy dates from 493 on both pages. This dossier ends at 499 to match Cliopatria's rows; if the Ostrogothic Kingdom dossier starts in 493, the two overlap in 493-499 and the orchestrator should trim this one to 492 and re-point the 'kingdom-of-odoacer' hand-over (its dissolve event already names 'ostrogoths' as counterpart). Discrepancies: Nedao 454 (Nedao and Ostrogoths pages) against 453 (Rugiland page); Theodemir's death 474 (Ostrogoths) against 475 (Theodemir page); treaty with Odoacer 2 February (Theodoric the Great) against 25 February (Odoacer). The Pannonian settlement date, Valamir and Videmir's reigns, and who held Pannonia after 474 are not on any page opened. The Sciri, Heruli and Theoderic Strabo's Goths (473-481) have no dossier here. Pages opened: six against a budget of five (Nedao was opened for both this dossier and Rugiland). No infobox area on any page. REVISION 2026-10-19 after review: (1) the 490-499 correction (120,380 km2, southern edge 43.76 N) is replaced by three keyframes, 490 (northern Italy but for Ravenna), 491-492 (plus Lilybaeum) and 493-499 (Italy less Sardinia, with Sicily, and Dalmatia, about 294,000 km2); the 493 gain from kingdom-of-odoacer is now the whole of Italy south of the 490 line, with Sicily and Dalmatia as two confidence-1 gains (no page dates their passing). (2) A 491 gain of Lilybaeum from vandal-kingdom (Gaiseric page footnote) mirrors vandal-kingdom /ledger/11. (3) The 474 and 479 'gains' from the Eastern Roman Empire and the 488 'loss' are now vassal_start and vassal_end events with counterpart eastern-roman-empire: the Goths were federates on imperial soil (Ostrogoths page, 'recognized as a federate kingdom' about 476), and the Empire's dossier has no loss. Disagreements: the vassal_start is dated 474, the entry, where eastern-roman-empire has 483 (Theodoric the Great page, magister militum praesentalis) and the Ostrogoths page 'about 476'; the Epirus pair is held coarsely to 488 because no page dates the departure. The Odoacer page's 'seized most of Italy by 490' would support a larger 490 shape than the north, but it names only Milan, Pavia and Ticinum and no city of the centre or south, so the south stays in the contested zone to March 493. (4) The 493-499 overlap with the Ostrogothic Kingdom (no dossier yet): see identity.successors; eastern-roman-empire's 493 vassal_start names ostrogothic-kingdom although Italy is this dossier's until 499, and its tint from 493 rests on the Ostrogothic Kingdom page's 'recognized by the new Emperor Anastasius in 497', which is why no vassalage is recorded here after 488. Pages opened in the revision: Ostrogothic Kingdom, Gaiseric, Odoacer (twice), Theodoric the Great, Ostrogoths, Vandal Kingdom; eight pages in all against a budget of five.
